## Summary

A short credit update precedes a full Meritage CEO interview recorded March 6. Eisman acknowledges his housing recommendation has suffered as rates rise, but retains a below-book, improving-capital-efficiency thesis. Philippe Lord describes affordability constraints, mortgage subsidies, local fees and the cost-benefit tradeoff in land options, then sets multiyear operating targets. Those targets belong to the CEO. Eisman separately endorses potential upside from higher ROE and a 1.5x book valuation, with rates and execution still decisive.

Claims are assessed individually. Empirical premises are not treated as successful forecasts. Unverified magnitudes and causal stories remain unresolved; subjective investment judgments are not assigned directional wins.

- [FSB warns on private-credit vulnerabilities](https://www.fsb.org/2026/05/fsb-warns-on-private-credit-vulnerabilities/) (2026-05-06): Identifies opaque valuations, lower-quality leveraged borrowers, sector concentration, layered leverage and bank/insurer linkages; notes rising PIK and some defaults. Report emphasizes data gaps and does not predict a completed systemic crisis.
- [Banking system conditions, June 2026 supervision report](https://www.federalreserve.gov/publications/2026-june-supervision-and-regulation-report-report-banking-system-conditions.htm) (2026-06-11): Q1 nonperforming-loan, loan-loss and reserve ratios declined slightly at most large banks. Q1 large-bank CET1 averaged 12% and all remained well capitalized. Data support current resilience, not a guarantee that future defaults cannot rise.

## Framework and tools

- Disaggregate housing demand into employment, affordability and confidence.
- Analyze land ownership, options and financing costs together.
- Connect operating margins, asset turns and ROE.
- Distinguish CEO targets from independent analyst forecasts.
- Keep recording dates separate from publication dates.

Tools and charts discussed, not a complete visual inspection:

- Meritage price/tangible-book range.
- Regional average selling prices and agency-loan eligibility.
- Mortgage-rate buydown mechanics.
- Owned versus optioned land and 12%-14% capital-partner charges.
- Three-to-five-year margin, ROE, growth and leverage targets.

## Source cautions

Steve Eisman hosts the opening wrap and interview, then offers closing conclusions. Philippe Lord, Meritage CEO, provides the corporate operating views and targets. Speaker switches were tracked through the full conversation.
- Full transcript read in two contiguous parts.
- Interview and post-interview conclusions explicitly dated March 6; opening wrap dated March 26.
- Philippe Lord is sometimes mistranscribed as Philip Lloyd; company name also varies in captions.
- FHA and Fannie/Freddie lending limits are conflated in discussion.
